sources.title: Introducing Amazon Nova: A New Generation of Foundation Models
sources.evidence: Dated December 3, 2024; explicitly says Nova Pro is generally available that day. Identifies Amazon as developer and Nova as the broader family, and specifies text/image/video input, text output, 300K context, and agentic/function-calling applications.

sources.title: Nova Pro — Amazon Bedrock
sources.evidence: Exact Nova Pro card maps the model to amazon.nova-pro-v1:0 and lists 300K context. Its December 5, 2024 launch-date field conflicts with Amazon's contemporaneous December 3 general-availability announcement.

sources.title: The Amazon Nova Family of Models: Technical Report and Model Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 for the parameter re-audit. Section 1.1 explicitly identifies Nova Pro, Lite, and Micro as Transformer-based. Reports Nova Pro capabilities and evaluation tables but does not disclose total or active parameter counts, nor dense versus MoE structure. This accessible author report was used after the Amazon-hosted PDF exceeded the browser fetch limit.

sources.title: Amazon Nova Premier: Technical Report and Model Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 for the parameter re-audit. April 30, 2025 addendum explicitly compares Nova Pro in capability and runtime tables. Those tables contain no total/active parameter counts or structural disclosure for Nova Pro.

sources.title: Amazon Nova 2: Multimodal Reasoning and Generation Models
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 for the parameter re-audit. Later first-party report includes explicitly labeled Nova 1 Pro comparisons, including multimodal benchmarks. No Nova 1 Pro total or active parameter count or dense/MoE classification is disclosed. Describes configurable extended thinking as introduced by Nova 2.

sources.title: Migrate from Amazon Nova 1 to Amazon Nova 2 on Amazon Bedrock
sources.evidence: March 18, 2026 version-specific table lists Nova 1 Pro: 300K context, text/image/video input, and Extended Thinking: No. Explains that configurable reasoning is a Nova 2 feature; contrasts built-in tools with existing external function calling.

sources.title: Complete request schema — Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Current shared schema says reasoningConfig applies to Amazon Nova Pro and Nova Lite, without an exact generation/model ID. This conflicts with the Nova 1 Pro migration table. The shared page also includes audio fields with an incomplete model applicability annotation, so it is insufficient to establish exact v1 capabilities alone.

sources.title: Iterative Training — Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Explicitly states Amazon Nova weights are proprietary. Explains customized checkpoints remain in escrow S3 buckets in AWS-managed accounts instead of being copied into the customer's account. This supplies concrete weight-access evidence, beyond API-only availability.

sources.title: Supervised Fine-Tuning — Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Explicitly identifies supported models as Nova 1.0 (Micro, Lite, Pro) and Nova 2.0 Lite, establishing the exact first-generation Pro's inclusion in the Nova customization documentation.

sources.title: Available foundation models — Amazon SageMaker AI
sources.evidence: The dated July 29, 2026 table explicitly lists Nova Pro, nova-textgeneration-pro, with license AWS Service Terms. The Nova rows appear under the general Open-Weight Models heading, conflicting with the direct proprietary-weight statement and escrow restrictions in the dedicated Nova training documentation; that heading is not treated as a public weight-release grant.

sources.title: AWS Service Terms
sources.evidence: Section 50.1 includes Amazon Foundation Models (Nova and Titan) among covered AI Services; section 50.10 explicitly includes Amazon Nova Pro. Supports the named service terms applicable to this proprietary model.

sources.title: Tool use (function calling) with Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Explicitly labeled Nova Version 1 documentation; describes defining external tools and returning tool results to the model. Combined with Nova Pro's own reported function-calling evaluation, establishes tool calling.

sources.title: Multimodal support for Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Explicitly labeled Nova Version 1 documentation. Describes image and video input, plus document inputs through Converse API, with PDF/DOCX processed as interleaved text and images.

sources.title: Models.dev Nova Pro v1 catalog record
sources.evidence: Original catalog lead: Nova Pro 1.0, nova-pro family key, December 5 release date, text/image input, and reasoning false. Its comments say metadata came from OpenRouter. Technical claims were checked independently against Amazon sources.

sources.title: Amazon-hosted Nova family technical report PDF
sources.evidence: The web fetch failed because the 21,232,147-byte document exceeded the fetch limit; the accessible author version on arXiv was read instead.

sources.title: What is Amazon Nova? — Version 1 model specifications
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 for the parameter re-audit. Exact Nova Pro column identifies amazon.nova-pro-v1:0, 300K context, text/image/video input, text output and PDF document support.

sources.title: MASSIVE-Agents: A Benchmark for Multilingual Function-Calling in 52 Languages
sources.evidence: Amazon AGI-authored EMNLP 2025 paper. Table 1 (PDF page 6) has an explicit Params column: the Nova Pro row is NP, with 300k context and December 2024 release, identifying first-generation Pro. The table supplies no numeric total or activated parameter count for Nova Pro; its other numeric columns are context, release date and output speed.

sources.title: PHLoRA: Data-Free Post-Hoc Low-Rank Adapter Extraction from Full-Rank Checkpoint
sources.evidence: December 2025 paper evaluates Nova Micro, Lite and Pro base models and full-rank/LoRA fine-tunes. Sections 4.1-4.3 and Tables 3-6 report adapter ranks 32, 64 and 512, performance and retained energy, not total or active model parameter counts. The named fine-tuning relationship does not supply a size-bearing base-model identity.

sources.title: Amazon Bedrock Model Distillation
sources.evidence: Explains that teacher-generated responses fine-tune a separately selected student; names Nova Premier as teacher and Nova Pro as student. This is knowledge distillation, not an assertion that Nova Pro shares the teacher parameter count or a named size-bearing base architecture.

sources.title: Benchmarking Generative AI for CSA Clause Extraction and CDM Representation
sources.evidence: May 2025 paper, appendix page 28, explicitly calls Nova Pro parameter count undisclosed and approximately 90B an estimate. Used only to investigate a secondary numeric lead, not as a developer specification.

sources.title: Amazon Nova (formerly Olympus)
sources.evidence: The summary explicitly labels all Nova parameter numbers as Alan estimates based on benchmark scores, including Nova Pro approximately 90B. This resolves the 90B lead as secondary estimation rather than developer-published nominal size or named-base lineage. No claim is made that the ISDA paper sourced this page.

sources.title: Architecting offline-first generative AI applications for edge deployments using AWS services
sources.evidence: July 22, 2026 first-party article names Nova Pro as a synthetic Q&A data generator, then specifies 21B total and 3.6B active for the separate gpt-oss-20b model fine-tuned on that data. Those numbers do not describe Nova Pro and provide no size-preserving model lineage.

name.note: The display name denotes the documented Nova 1.0 Pro variant, with AWS model ID amazon.nova-pro-v1:0; this is not Nova 2 Pro or Nova Premier.

developer.note: Amazon's launch announcement and Amazon AGI-authored technical report establish the developer.

family.note: Nova is the model family; Pro is its tier. Normalized to the shared catalog family key.

release_date.note: The December 3 announcement explicitly says Nova Pro is generally available today. The Bedrock card currently lists December 5, but that later metadata date cannot supersede the earlier contemporaneous public release. Provider-specific December 5 metadata is not used as model release.

open_weights.note: Dedicated Nova training documentation explicitly calls the weights proprietary and describes AWS-controlled escrow checkpoints; the supported-model list includes Nova 1.0 Pro. The broad JumpStart table's Open-Weight heading is inconsistent with this specific access policy and provides no Nova download or redistribution grant.

license.note: The exact Nova Pro JumpStart row names AWS Service Terms, and those terms expressly cover Nova Pro. This is the service license/terms designation, not an open-weight license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review reopened the original Nova family report, Premier and Nova 2 comparison reports, and exact v1 specification page, then searched for newer total/active disclosures and size-bearing lineage. Amazon AGI MASSIVE-Agents Table 1 explicitly marks Nova Pro Params as NP. PHLoRA gives adapter ranks, not base-model size; distillation documentation does not establish parameter-preserving lineage. The approximately 90B lead is explicitly a secondary benchmark-based estimate, and the later AWS 21B figure belongs to gpt-oss-20b. No developer nominal total or size-bearing named base was established.

active_parameters_b.note: Checked active/activated count separately in the reopened original, Premier and Nova 2 reports and later Amazon-authored MASSIVE-Agents and PHLoRA comparisons. None supplies an activated-parameter column or count for Nova Pro. MASSIVE-Agents Params is NP; PHLoRA adapter ranks do not imply active size. A July 2026 AWS article reports 3.6B active only for gpt-oss-20b trained on Nova-generated data. No Nova Pro active count or dense/MoE classification was established.

architecture.note: Section 1.1 expressly says Nova Pro, Lite, and Micro are based on Transformer architecture. It does not establish dense versus MoE, layer counts, or other structural details.

context_window.note: Both the launch announcement and exact Nova Pro card report 300K tokens; the later Nova 1 Pro comparison confirms 300K. This is documented context capacity, not a live endpoint test.

modalities.note: Text/image/video inputs and text output are explicit. PDF document support is available through Converse and is retained as a catalog input format.

reasoning.note: Unresolved first-party conflict: the March 2026 table explicitly says Nova 1 Pro has no Extended Thinking, while the current shared request schema claims reasoningConfig for Nova Pro and Nova Lite without exact version IDs. Nova 2's report calls extended thinking a new feature. Ordinary prompted reasoning is established, but current dedicated reasoning-mode support for amazon.nova-pro-v1:0 cannot be treated as unambiguously verified from these conflicting documents.

tool_call.note: Original and Premier reports evaluate Nova Pro on function calling; the version-1 API documentation specifies tool-use messages and responses. Lack of Nova 2-style built-in tools does not mean external tool calling is absent.

description.value: Amazon Nova Pro 1.0 is a multimodal Transformer with a 300K-token context window, document and video inputs, and tool calling.
description.note: Replaces the unsupported/currently misleading flagship label and broad production-workflow claim with exact documented model properties.

patch.description: Amazon Nova Pro 1.0 is a multimodal Transformer with a 300K-token context window, document and video inputs, and tool calling.
patch.notes: Total and active parameters remain undisclosed; Amazon AGI’s MASSIVE-Agents table marks Nova Pro Params as NP. The reported 90B estimate is secondary and benchmark-based. Dense/MoE structure is unspecified. Amazon announced general availability on December 3, 2024; the Bedrock card's December 5 date conflicts. Reasoning-mode support remains unresolved: AWS's Nova 1 Pro migration table says no extended thinking, while its current shared schema claims reasoningConfig for Nova Pro without an exact generation ID. Dedicated Nova training documentation explicitly identifies proprietary weights and AWS-managed escrow storage despite the broad JumpStart table's inconsistent Open-Weight heading.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains explicit null total/active counts after reopening original and later first-party reports, checking Amazon AGI MASSIVE-Agents Params=NP and PHLoRA adapter-rank tables, and resolving secondary 90B and unrelated gpt-oss-20b size leads. No size-bearing lineage or active-count disclosure was found. All nonparameter assessments are preserved, including the original release-date and reasoning-support qualifications.
